newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish archaeologists find 7,000-year old canoe.
newsitem.headline: Irish archaeologists find 7,000-year old canoe.

text.p: A 7,000-year-old wooden canoe, found in the mud flats of the Shannon estuary in the west of Ireland, may be one of the oldest signs of a human settlement in the country.
Carbon-dating methods show the mesolithic wooden craft dates back to 4,800 BC and is about 2,000 years older than other canoes found by archaeologists in Ireland.
"The marks of the stone tools used to carve the boat can still be seen on areas of the wood," Ronan O'Flaherty, manager of the discovery programme, said.
The canoe, preserved by the silt, was found near a bank of the Shannon river directly opposite Bunratty Castle, a tourist attraction in County Clare.
Also located in the same operation were a piece of human skull, which has been sent for dating to experts in Britain, flint tools, a fish-trap and other relics.
